answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require proof of sustained useful work before reputation counts: new identities start as a faint ember with zero weight, and only verified attestations over time raise them toward the zenith of full trust. A gale of fresh clones then costs real compute and history to fake, because weight accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk; clones that never do honest work stay weightless, so flooding the network stops paying.
